The world's best archer can be beaten by a blindfold.

Kevin Trudeau tells a story from his first speech in the 80s, shared with Zig Ziglar. Zig said he could beat the greatest archer alive every time. All he had to do was blindfold him.

Kevin thought that was silly. How can anyone hit a target he can't see? Zig's answer: most people live life trying to hit a target they don't have.

What is the target you could name right now?

#ad #goals #success #mindset

Success has a price, and so does failure.

Kevin Trudeau hears it all the time: it will take three years before I see results. His reply is simple. If you don't do it, three years from now you still won't see any results. Three years pass anyway.

He remembers a man asking how old he would be in five years. Kevin asked how old he'd be if he did nothing. Same age, same age, same age, just broker.

Where will you be in three years if nothing changes?

#ad #success #mindset #habits

Garbage in, garbage out applies to your mind too.

Kevin Trudeau points out that guys who work out are fanatical about what they put in their bodies. They count carbs, fats and protein and plan every meal.

But the mind, he says, is the biggest muscle in the body. And most people feed it garbage, the old computer rule: garbage in, garbage out.

What did you feed your mind today?

#ad #mindset #success #habits

They slept in the back of the restaurant. Now they're rich.

Kevin Trudeau worked in a restaurant owned by a Greek man and asked how he became successful. His family left Greece, worked in restaurants and slept in the back. They saved to bring over the rest of the family, then bought their own restaurant, and kept saving and working seven days a week.

Then a house. Then a bigger restaurant. That, Kevin says, is the American dream.

What are you willing to do first, before the reward comes?

#ad #wealth #business #success

Are you comparing yourself to the wrong people?

Kevin Trudeau says his mother's dream was a happy family and a house full of well-fed people. She woke up every day thinking, I love my life.

His own answer was different. He wanted more, because he felt he could create more.

His definition of success: not what you've done compared to what others have done, but what you've done compared to what you could have done.

When did you last feel you were on purpose?

#ad #success #goals #happiness

Being nice isn't the same as being decisive.

Kevin Trudeau walks into a restaurant and takes charge. He gives his name with a smile. If he doesn't like the table, he asks for another one. He knows what he wants and says it pleasantly.

He says he isn't arrogant and he isn't a jerk. He is very pleasant, but decisive. And the people around him notice.

When did you last ask for exactly what you wanted?

#ad #relationships #confidence #love

Kevin's mother warned him he'd turn out just like them. That was the point.

Kevin Trudeau grew up in Boston listening to audio tapes by Zig Ziglar and Earl Nightingale. His mother got mad and said he would turn out like those people.

He agreed. Everyone says don't hang around the bad crowd because you'll turn out like them. If that's true, Kevin says, then hanging around the success crowd makes you turn out like them.

Who are you becoming like right now?

#ad #success #mindset #habits

What if hating to lose beats loving to win?

Kevin Trudeau talked with a man who won six Super Bowls. He said he loves winning and craves it. But something is even more powerful: hating to lose. He hates losing more than he wants to win.

Kevin calls that the why behind the why. We are driven either by a desire for pleasure or by a desire to avoid pain, and the second is stronger.

What do you refuse to put up with in your life?

#ad #success #mindset #goals

Where do successful people put their time and money first?

Kevin Trudeau says Warren Buffett has said that all successful people, when they start off, invest most of their money and time in personal development. It pays the biggest dividends for the longest period.

Kevin explains that training isn't only the gym. It's training your mind and your habits. Most people's habits are failure habits, not success habits.

What habit would you train first?

He wasn't the best-looking man in the room. He loved being himself.

Kevin Trudeau knew a slight, not very articulate man who was always with superstar-looking women. His secret was one sentence: I love being me.

He wasn't trying to be someone else. He had a great relationship with himself, and that confidence oozed out of him. He had lots of friends and a good career without chasing big goals.

When did you last wake up thinking, I love being me?
